chunks.title: Acute Hypoxaemic Respiratory Failure — Local Reference Note
chunks.text:
# Acute Hypoxaemic Respiratory Failure — Local Reference Note PROVENANCE: Local reference note authored for the MedExplain AI research prototype. This is NOT a published guideline, NOT a verbatim society document, and carries NO
PMID or DOI. It is included so the retrieval pipeline has real, citable-in-system
material to search. Any clinical use requires verification against the current
published source. ## Definition Acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure is a state of inadequate oxygenation
(commonly defined as PaO2 < 60 mmHg or SpO2 < 90%) with elevated work of
breathing, developing over hours to days. It is distinguished from chronic
respiratory failure by the abrupt onset and by the absence of a chronic
compensatory pattern. ## Assessment Oxygenation is assessed by the PaO2/FiO2 (P/F) ratio:

chunks.title: Acute Hypoxaemic Respiratory Failure — Local Reference Note
chunks.text:
failure by the abrupt onset and by the absence of a chronic
compensatory pattern. ## Assessment Oxygenation is assessed by the PaO2/FiO2 (P/F) ratio:
- P/F > 300: no acute lung injury
- P/F 200-300 with PEEP >= 5 cmH2O: mild acute respiratory distress
- P/F 100-200 with PEEP >= 5 cmH2O: moderate acute respiratory distress
- P/F <= 100 with PEEP >= 5 cmH2O: severe acute respiratory distress The P/F ratio requires an arterial (or reliably arterialised) PaO2 and an
inspired oxygen fraction. A saturation-based SpO2/FIO2 ratio is a reasonable
screening surrogate in some settings but is not equivalent to the P/F ratio and
has different calibration limits. ## Differentiating the mechanism Two broad mechanism groups must be separated: 1. Cardiogenic (hydrostatic) pulmonary oedema — raised left atrial pressure. Supporting features include cardiomegaly, perihilar alveolar distribution,
   Kerley B lines, pleural effusions, and elevated natriuretic peptides. 2. Non-cardiogenic oedema — increased capillary permeability.

chunks.title: Acute Hypoxaemic Respiratory Failure — Local Reference Note
chunks.text:
r distribution,
   Kerley B lines, pleural effusions, and elevated natriuretic peptides. 2. Non-cardiogenic oedema — increased capillary permeability.
Supporting features
   include a normal cardiac silhouette, peripheral or basal ground-glass
   attenuation, absence of Kerley B lines, and preserved ventricular indices. No single feature is definitive. Interpretation must combine the physiological
data, the imaging appearance, and the clinical trajectory. ## Inflammatory markers Serum C-reactive protein is a non-specific acute-phase reactant. An elevated
value indicates an inflammatory response but does not identify its cause, and it
does not by itself distinguish infectious from inflammatory from non-inflammatory
processes. It is useful for trend monitoring, not for diagnosis. ## Cardiac injury markers

chunks.title: Acute Hypoxaemic Respiratory Failure — Local Reference Note
chunks.text:
tinguish infectious from inflammatory from non-inflammatory
processes. It is useful for trend monitoring, not for diagnosis. ## Cardiac injury markers
A normal troponin at presentation reduces the likelihood of acute myocardial
injury but does not exclude it: early presenters may still be troponin-negative
before the biomarker rises, and a normal value carries no exclusionary weight
after several hours of ischaemia. ## Escalation Sustained hypoxaemia despite oxygen, increasing work of breathing, or
haemodynamic instability warrants urgent senior and critical-care review. Oxygen
therapy targets are individualised; a common working target in adults without
known hypercapnic respiratory failure is SpO2 92-96%.

chunks.title: COPD Exacerbation — Local Reference Note
chunks.text:
# COPD Exacerbation — Local Reference Note PROVENANCE: Local reference note authored for the MedExplain AI research prototype. Not a published guideline, not a verbatim society document, no PMID or DOI. Included so the retrieval pipeline has real local material to search. ## Definition A COPD exacerbation is an **acute worsening of respiratory symptoms** — increased
dyspnoea, increased sputum volume, or increased sputum purulence — that is
acute in onset and requires a change in regular medication. The cardinal point
is the *change from baseline*: a patient breathing normally at their usual
sputum volume with a chronic baseline dyspnoea is not, by definition, in
exacerbation. ## Anthracosis and chronic parenchymal change Anthracosis is the accumulation of carbon pigment in lung tissue, usually
peribronchial. On plain radiography it manifests as:

chunks.title: COPD Exacerbation — Local Reference Note
chunks.text:
onic parenchymal change Anthracosis is the accumulation of carbon pigment in lung tissue, usually
peribronchial. On plain radiography it manifests as:
- fine nodular or reticulonodular opacities, predominantly **upper lobe**
- more prominent with advancing age
- co-existing hyperinflation: flattened hemidiaphragms, increased retrosternal
  airspace, horizontally oriented ribs, reduced peripheral vascular markings Anthracosis is a *nonspecific marker of long-term particulate exposure*,
frequently co-dated. It is associated with but not specific to COPD, and it does
not by itself establish COPD as the cause of an acute presentation. ## Hyperinflation The radiographic features of hyperinflation are listed above. Important
caveat: hyperinflation is **also** seen in asthma and in obesity, and it can be
over-estimated by poor inspiratory effort and by AP projection. ## Gas exchange Exacerbations frequently cause hypoxaemia with or without a raised PaCO2.

chunks.title: COPD Exacerbation — Local Reference Note
chunks.text:
r-estimated by poor inspiratory effort and by AP projection. ## Gas exchange Exacerbations frequently cause hypoxaemia with or without a raised PaCO2.
A normal PaCO2 in a patient with a known history of hypercapnic failure is
alarming rather than reassuring, because it may represent over-ventilation from
hypoxaemia. PaCO2 must be interpreted against the patient's own baseline. ## Inflammatory markers C-reactive protein often rises during exacerbations, particularly those with
purulent sputum. Elevated CRP has been associated with a longer time to
recovery in some cohorts, but it is not sufficiently specific to guide
antibiotic use on its own; sputum purulence and clinical assessment remain the
primary drivers of the antibiotic decision. ## Antibiotic stewardship Antibiotics are most clearly indicated when all three cardinal features are
present (increased dyspnoea, increased sputum volume, increased sputum purulence)
or when two are present with one being purulence, or when mechanical
ventilation is required.

chunks.title: COPD Exacerbation — Local Reference Note
chunks.text:
ea, increased sputum volume, increased sputum purulence)
or when two are present with one being purulence, or when mechanical
ventilation is required.
Inpatient cultures — particularly blood cultures —
are obtained before treatment in severe exacerbations. De-escalation should be
planned from the outset.

chunks.title: Evidence Retrieval and Citation Integrity — System Design Note
chunks.text:
# Evidence Retrieval and Citation Integrity — System Design Note PROVENANCE: Local design note authored for the MedExplain AI research prototype. This document is **about the system itself**, not about medicine. No PMID or DOI. ## Purpose This note records the rules the MedExplain AI retrieval layer enforces, so that
the behaviour is auditable and so that reviewers can verify that no citation is
ever produced that is not traceable to a stored local document. ## Rules enforced by the pipeline 1. **No citation without a source.** Every evidence item returned by
   `POST /api/retrieve/evidence` corresponds to a specific chunk of a specific
   document in the local knowledge directory. There is no generative path that
   can invent a reference. 2. **Identifiers are validated, not trusted.** Only identifiers that match the
   issued pattern are accepted as grounding targets.

chunks.title: Evidence Retrieval and Citation Integrity — System Design Note
chunks.text:
nvent a reference. 2. **Identifiers are validated, not trusted.** Only identifiers that match the
   issued pattern are accepted as grounding targets.
A model that produces
   `[doc:some-thing-not-issued]` has that reference dropped and the response
   marked as insufficiently grounded. 3. **Empty index is a first-class state.** When the knowledge base is not
   initialized, the API returns `Knowledge base not initialized` and an empty
   evidence list. It does **not** fall back to model-recalled references. 4. **Local notes carry no external identifiers.** The documents in
   `backend/data/knowledge/` are local reference notes authored for this
   prototype. They deliberately carry **no PMID and no DOI**, because no
   published identifier was verified. A note that asserted one would be a
   fabricated citation. 5. **Similarity scores are not evidence of clinical truth.** A cosine similarity
   is a measure of embedding proximity, nothing more. It carries no clinical
   meaning and is not a confidence. 6.

chunks.title: Evidence Retrieval and Citation Integrity — System Design Note
chunks.text:
nical truth.** A cosine similarity
   is a measure of embedding proximity, nothing more. It carries no clinical
   meaning and is not a confidence. 6.
**Grounding is necessary, not sufficient.** A citation that resolves proves
   only that the text exists in the local store. It does not prove the retrieved
   text answers the question asked. ## What the retrieval layer deliberately does not do - It does not query PubMed, Crossref, or any network service. - It does not perform web search to fill an empty index. - It does not let the language model add references that retrieval did not
  return. - It does not report recall, precision, or any retrieval quality metric, because
  none has been measured against a labelled query set. ## Verification procedure To confirm the system honours these rules: 1. Start with an empty index and query. Expect an explicit not-initialized
   response and zero evidence items. 2. Ingest documents, restart, query. Expect evidence items whose `source` and
   `document_id` match ingested files. 3.

Ask the model directly for a citation with no supporting retrieval. Expect

chunks.title: WHO CNS 5 Diffuse Glioma Classification and Multiparametric MRI Staging
chunks.text:
# WHO CNS 5 Diffuse Glioma Classification and Multiparametric MRI Staging PROVENANCE: Local reference note authored for the MedExplain AI research prototype. Ground truth for multimodal brain disease clinical decision support. Citable within system. ## Diagnostic Definition and Pathophysiology
Diffuse gliomas constitute the most common primary intra-axial neuroepithelial neoplasms of the central nervous system. Under the WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (5th Edition, WHO CNS 5), classification integrates molecular profiling (IDH1/2 mutation status, 1p/19q codeletion, ATRX loss, TERT promoter mutation, CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion) with histological features. - **Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype (WHO Grade 4)**: Hallmark features include microvascular proliferation, pseudopalisading necrosis, and aggressive parenchymal infiltration.

chunks.title: WHO CNS 5 Diffuse Glioma Classification and Multiparametric MRI Staging
chunks.text:
H-wildtype (WHO Grade 4)**: Hallmark features include microvascular proliferation, pseudopalisading necrosis, and aggressive parenchymal infiltration.
- **Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant (WHO Grade 2, 3, or 4)**: Graded based on mitotic activity and CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion. - **Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted (WHO Grade 2 or 3)**. ## Neuroimaging Hallmarks (Multiparametric MRI)
1. **T1-Weighted Post-Gadolinium**:
   - High-grade gliomas characteristically demonstrate thick, irregular, nodular ring enhancement surrounding a central non-enhancing hypointense necrotic core. - Low-grade gliomas typically demonstrate minimal or no contrast enhancement. 2. **T2/FLAIR Hyperintensity**:
   - Extensive non-enhancing infiltrative signal abnormality representing a combination of vasogenic edema and non-enhancing infiltrative neoplastic glial cells. - Distinct from pure vasogenic edema; infiltrative glioma cells extend well beyond visible contrast enhancement into adjacent white matter tracts. 3.

chunks.title: WHO CNS 5 Diffuse Glioma Classification and Multiparametric MRI Staging
chunks.text:
- Distinct from pure vasogenic edema; infiltrative glioma cells extend well beyond visible contrast enhancement into adjacent white matter tracts. 3.
**Mass Effect and Hemispheric Asymmetry**:
   - Compression of adjacent sulci, ipsilateral lateral ventricle effacement, midline shift (>5 mm predicts herniation risk), and subfalcine or uncal herniation vectors. 4. **Diffusion-Weighted Imaging (DWI/ADC)**:
   - High cellularity zones demonstrate restricted water diffusion with hypointensity on Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (ADC) maps. 5. **Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (MRS)**:
   - Markedly elevated Choline (Cho) to N-acetylaspartate (NAA) ratio (Cho/NAA > 2.0), reduced NAA (neuronal loss), and elevated Lipid-Lactate peak reflecting anaerobic metabolism/necrosis. ## Clinical Symptom Presentation
- **Progressive Headache**: Morning worsening, valsalva exacerbation, signs of increased intracranial pressure (ICP).

chunks.title: WHO CNS 5 Diffuse Glioma Classification and Multiparametric MRI Staging
chunks.text:
## Clinical Symptom Presentation
- **Progressive Headache**: Morning worsening, valsalva exacerbation, signs of increased intracranial pressure (ICP).
- **New-Onset Epileptic Seizures**: Focal seizures with or without secondary generalization; common presenting sign in cortical and subcortical locations. - **Focal Neurological Deficits**: Hemiparesis, dysphasia/aphasia, sensory disturbances corresponding to lesion topography. - **Cognitive and Executive Decline**: Frontal lobe syndrome, psychomotor slowing, apathy, acoustic/phonetic speech pauses. ## Clinical Decision Support Directives
1. Urgently schedule 3-Tesla volumetric neuronavigation MRI with multiplanar thin-slice T1+C, T2/FLAIR, DWI, and perfusion (DSC-MRI rCBV). 2. Initiate corticosteroid therapy (Dexamethasone) for symptomatic mass effect and perilesional vasogenic edema with gastric prophylaxis. 3. Urgent Neurosurgical Oncology evaluation for stereotactic biopsy vs maximal safe resection with intraoperative neuromonitoring (fMRI / DTI tractography). 4.

chunks.title: WHO CNS 5 Diffuse Glioma Classification and Multiparametric MRI Staging
chunks.text:
Neurosurgical Oncology evaluation for stereotactic biopsy vs maximal safe resection with intraoperative neuromonitoring (fMRI / DTI tractography). 4.
Neurological consultation for anti-seizure medication (ASM) initiation if seizures or high epileptogenic location.

chunks.title: Meningioma Grading, Morphologic Radiomics, and Dural Attachment Diagnostics
chunks.text:
# Meningioma Grading, Morphologic Radiomics, and Dural Attachment Diagnostics PROVENANCE: Local reference note authored for the MedExplain AI research prototype. Ground truth for multimodal brain disease clinical decision support. Citable within system. ## Diagnostic Definition and Epidemiology
Meningiomas are the most frequent primary extra-axial non-glial intracranial neoplasms, originating from meningothelial arachnoid cap cells of the arachnoid villi. - **WHO Grade 1 (Benign)**: ~80-85% of cases (Meningothelial, fibrous, transitional subtypes); slow-growing, circumscribed. - **WHO Grade 2 (Atypical)**: ~15-20% of cases (Increased mitoses >= 4/10 HPF, spontaneous necrosis, sheeting, prominent nucleoli, brain invasion); higher recurrence rate.

chunks.title: Meningioma Grading, Morphologic Radiomics, and Dural Attachment Diagnostics
chunks.text:
ical)**: ~15-20% of cases (Increased mitoses >= 4/10 HPF, spontaneous necrosis, sheeting, prominent nucleoli, brain invasion); higher recurrence rate.
- **WHO Grade 3 (Anaplastic/Malignant)**: ~1-3% of cases (Rhabdoid, papillary, frank sarcomatous/carcinomatous morphology, >= 20 mitoses/10 HPF). ## Neuroimaging Characteristics (MRI & CT)
1. **Extra-Axial Signs**:
   - Broad-based dural attachment with the classic pathognomonic **"Dural Tail Sign"** (thickening and avid enhancement of adjacent tapering dura mater). - CSF cleft sign (thin rim of cerebrospinal fluid interposed between the mass and displaced cerebral parenchyma). - Cortical buckling and inward displacement of cortical gray matter and pial vessels. 2. **Signal Characteristics**:
   - **T1-Weighted**: Iso- to slightly hypointense relative to cortex. - **T2/FLAIR**: Iso- to hyperintense. Hyperintensity on T2 often correlates with increased vascularity or soft/syncytial subtype.

chunks.title: Meningioma Grading, Morphologic Radiomics, and Dural Attachment Diagnostics
chunks.text:
relative to cortex. - **T2/FLAIR**: Iso- to hyperintense. Hyperintensity on T2 often correlates with increased vascularity or soft/syncytial subtype.
- **Post-Contrast T1**: Intensely, uniformly, and homogeneously enhancing mass with sharply circumscribed boundaries. 3. **Bony Remodeling (CT/MRI)**:
   - Hyperostosis of adjacent cranial vault (particularly in convex, parasagittal, sphenoid wing, and olfactory groove meningiomas). - Bony erosion or osteolysis is more suggestive of atypical (Grade 2) or malignant (Grade 3) histology. 4. **Perilesional Edema**:
   - Variable vasogenic edema in adjacent brain parenchyma, driven by vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) secretion and cortical pial supply recruitment. ## Differential Diagnosis
- Dural metastases (prostate, breast, melanoma). - Solitary fibrous tumor / Hemangiopericytoma (lack of hyperostosis, prominent flow voids, staghorn vasculature). - Schwannoma (cerebellopontine angle location with expansion of internal auditory canal). - Neurosarcoidosis / Pachymeningitis.

chunks.title: Meningioma Grading, Morphologic Radiomics, and Dural Attachment Diagnostics
chunks.text:
staghorn vasculature). - Schwannoma (cerebellopontine angle location with expansion of internal auditory canal). - Neurosarcoidosis / Pachymeningitis.
## Clinical Recommendations & Protocol
1. Contrast-enhanced MRI with high-resolution volumetric 3D T1-SPGR/MPRAGE and coronal reconstruction. 2. Assess venous sinus patency (MR Venography / CTV) if tumor abuts superior sagittal sinus or transverse/sigmoid sinus (Simpson Grade planning). 3. Observation with serial volumetric imaging for asymptomatic, small, calcified incidental Grade 1 meningiomas. 4. Neurosurgical resection (maximal safe Simpson resection) or stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS/Gamma Knife) for enlarging, symptomatic, or skull base lesions with cranial nerve impingement.

chunks.title: Normal Brain Neuroanatomy, Differential Diagnostic Framework and Pseudolesions
chunks.text:
# Normal Brain Neuroanatomy, Differential Diagnostic Framework and Pseudolesions PROVENANCE: Local reference note authored for the MedExplain AI research prototype. Ground truth for multimodal brain disease clinical decision support. Citable within system. ## Normal Brain MRI Morphology (Negative Control Parameters)
1. **Symmetry & Ventricular Configuration**:
   - Lateral ventricles symmetrical in volume, morphology, and fronto-occipital horns without effacement, hydrocephalus, or dilation. - Third and fourth ventricles in normal midline anatomical alignment without lateral displacement or downward transtentorial pressure. - Symmetrical hemispheric sulcation and cortical thickness appropriate for patient age. 2.

chunks.title: Normal Brain Neuroanatomy, Differential Diagnostic Framework and Pseudolesions
chunks.text:
t lateral displacement or downward transtentorial pressure. - Symmetrical hemispheric sulcation and cortical thickness appropriate for patient age. 2.
**Gray-White Matter Junction**:
   - Preserved demarcation between deep cortical ribbon (gray matter) and subcortical white matter without blurring, loss of contrast, or focal dedifferentiation. 3. **Midline Structures**:
   - Preserved midline interhemispheric falx cerebri with 0.0 mm midline shift. - Optic chiasm, pituitary gland in sella turcica, brainstem (midbrain, pons, medulla), and cerebellar vermis normal in volume and signal characteristics. 4. **Signal Intensity Baselines**:
   - Normal physiological CSF is homogenously dark (suppressed) on T2/FLAIR and bright on standard T2. - Absence of pathological restricted diffusion on DWI (normal b=1000 and corresponding ADC map values 700-800 x 10^-6 mm^2/s). - Absence of abnormal leptomeningeal, pachymeningeal, intra-axial nodular, or ring enhancement following intravenous gadolinium.

chunks.title: Normal Brain Neuroanatomy, Differential Diagnostic Framework and Pseudolesions
chunks.text:
-800 x 10^-6 mm^2/s). - Absence of abnormal leptomeningeal, pachymeningeal, intra-axial nodular, or ring enhancement following intravenous gadolinium.
## Differential Diagnostic Framework for Intracranial Mass Lesions
When an intracranial lesion or signal abnormality is identified, multiparametric evaluation distinguishes between primary neoplastic and non-neoplastic mimics:
- **Intra-Axial vs Extra-Axial**:
  - Intra-axial: Glioma, metastasis, primary CNS lymphoma, cerebral abscess, acute cerebral infarction, tumefactive demyelination. - Extra-axial: Meningioma, schwannoma, epidermoid cyst, pituitary macroadenoma, arachnoid cyst. - **Ring Enhancement Differential (MAGIC DR mnemonic)**:
  - **M**: Metastasis (well-circumscribed, profound vasogenic edema out of proportion to tumor volume, gray-white junction). - **A**: Abscess (smooth thin rim, dual-rim sign on T2, central restricted diffusion on DWI with low ADC). - **G**: Glioblastoma (irregular, nodular, thick ragged ring with central necrosis and infiltrative FLAIR rim).

chunks.title: Normal Brain Neuroanatomy, Differential Diagnostic Framework and Pseudolesions
chunks.text:
ricted diffusion on DWI with low ADC). - **G**: Glioblastoma (irregular, nodular, thick ragged ring with central necrosis and infiltrative FLAIR rim).
- **I**: Infarct (subacute luxury perfusion, gyriform enhancement conforming to vascular territory). - **C**: Contusion / Hematoma (evolution of hemoglobin breakdown products, hemosiderin blooming on SWI/GRE). - **D**: Demyelinating lesion / Tumefactive MS (open-ring or incomplete horseshoe enhancement facing the cortex). - **R**: Radiation necrosis (soap-bubble or Swiss-cheese enhancement in previously irradiated field). ## Multimodal Decision Support Recommendations
1. For confirmed normal brain MRI scans in symptomatic patients (headache, dizziness, transient ischemic attacks), investigate metabolic, cervical, vestibular, vascular, or functional etiologies. 2. Consider dynamic MR Angiography (MRA) or CT Angiography (CTA) if acute neurovascular symptoms persist despite normal parenchymal MRI. 3.

chunks.title: Normal Brain Neuroanatomy, Differential Diagnostic Framework and Pseudolesions
chunks.text:
tiologies. 2. Consider dynamic MR Angiography (MRA) or CT Angiography (CTA) if acute neurovascular symptoms persist despite normal parenchymal MRI. 3.
Schedule 3- to 6-month surveillance imaging if clinical suspicion for early or microscopic epileptogenic focus remains elevated.

chunks.title: Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors (PitNET) and Sellar Region Pathologies
chunks.text:
# Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors (PitNET) and Sellar Region Pathologies PROVENANCE: Local reference note authored for the MedExplain AI research prototype. Ground truth for multimodal brain disease clinical decision support. Citable within system. ## Diagnostic Definition and Classification
Pituitary adenomas, classified in current nomenclature as Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors (PitNETs), originate from adenohypophyseal cells of the anterior pituitary gland within the sella turcica. - **Classification by Size**:
  - **Microadenoma**: Maximum diameter < 10 mm (confined to sella, rarely produces mass effect, presents via endocrine hypersecretion). - **Macroadenoma**: Maximum diameter >= 10 mm (often extends suprasellar into optic chiasm or parasellar into cavernous sinus). - **Giant Adenoma**: Maximum diameter >= 40 mm.

chunks.title: Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors (PitNET) and Sellar Region Pathologies
chunks.text:
um diameter >= 10 mm (often extends suprasellar into optic chiasm or parasellar into cavernous sinus). - **Giant Adenoma**: Maximum diameter >= 40 mm.
- **Classification by Functional Status**:
  - Non-functioning pituitary adenomas (NFPA): ~30-40% (silent gonadotroph; present with mass effect). - Prolactinomas (PRL-secreting): ~40-50% (galactorrhea, amenorrhea, hypogonadism). - Somatotroph adenomas (GH-secreting): ~10-15% (acromegaly / gigantism). - Corticotroph adenomas (ACTH-secreting): ~5-10% (Cushing disease). - Thyrotroph adenomas (TSH-secreting): <1%. ## Multiparametric Sellar MRI Protocol
1. **Dedicated Thin-Slice Sellar Protocol**:
   - High-resolution coronal and sagittal T1- and T2-weighted sequences (<= 2 mm slice thickness). - Dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) coronal T1 imaging with early arterial phase to detect microadenomas (which enhance more slowly than normal pituitary gland). 2. **Macroadenoma Appearance**:
   - Expansion and ballooning of the bony sella turcica with remodeling of the sellar floor.

chunks.title: Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors (PitNET) and Sellar Region Pathologies
chunks.text:
normal pituitary gland). 2. **Macroadenoma Appearance**:
   - Expansion and ballooning of the bony sella turcica with remodeling of the sellar floor.
- Suprasellar extension through the diaphragma sellae creating a characteristic **"Figure-of-8" or "Snowman" sign** due to waist compression. - Upward displacement, stretching, and thinning of the optic chiasm. 3. **Cavernous Sinus Infiltration (Knosp Classification)**:
   - Evaluated by tumor relation to the internal carotid artery (ICA) flow voids:
     - Knosp Grade 0-1: Medial to intercarotid tangent line (low invasion probability). - Knosp Grade 2: Crosses intercarotid tangent but medial to lateral tangent. - Knosp Grade 3-4: Encases ICA with total lateral extension (predicts subtotal resection). 4. **Pituitary Apoplexy**:
   - Acute infarction or hemorrhage within a preexisting adenoma: intrinsic T1 hyperintensity (methemoglobin), fluid-debris levels, acute severe headache, and cranial nerve III/IV/VI palsies.

chunks.title: Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors (PitNET) and Sellar Region Pathologies
chunks.text:
n a preexisting adenoma: intrinsic T1 hyperintensity (methemoglobin), fluid-debris levels, acute severe headache, and cranial nerve III/IV/VI palsies.
## Visual and Endocrine Consequences
- **Bitemporal Hemianopsia**: Classic visual field deficit resulting from selective compression of crossing nasal retinal fibers in the optic chiasm. - **Optic Neuropathy**: Reduced visual acuity, afferent pupillary defect, optic disc pallor. - **Hypopituitarism**: Secondary adrenal insufficiency, central hypothyroidism, gonadotropin deficiency. ## Clinical Protocol & Recommendations
1. Dedicated high-resolution pituitary protocol MRI (coronal dynamic T1, thin T2, post-gadolinium). 2. Formal automated visual field testing (Humphrey / Goldmann visual perimetry). 3. Complete baseline pituitary hormonal panel (Serum Prolactin, IGF-1, 8 AM Cortisol, ACTH, Free T4, TSH, LH, FSH, Testosterone/Estradiol). 4. If prolactinoma is confirmed, medical therapy with dopamine agonists (Cabergoline) is initial first-line therapy. 5.

chunks.text:
FSH, Testosterone/Estradiol). 4. If prolactinoma is confirmed, medical therapy with dopamine agonists (Cabergoline) is initial first-line therapy. 5.
Endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal surgical decompression for chiasmatic compression, visual field compromise, apoplexy, or non-prolactinoma macroadenomas.

chunks.title: Pneumonia and Pulmonary Oedema — Differential Discrimination
chunks.text:
# Pneumonia and Pulmonary Oedema — Differential Discrimination PROVENANCE: Local reference note authored for the MedExplain AI research prototype. Not a published article, not a society guideline, no PMID or DOI. Included so the retrieval pipeline has real local material to search. ## The core problem Pneumonia and cardiogenic pulmonary oedema are both common causes of acute
bilateral opacities with hypoxaemia, and they frequently overlap. Discriminating
them is one of the highest-value judgements in acute chest medicine, and one of
the most frequently made incorrectly. ## Findings favouring cardiogenic oedema

chunks.title: Pneumonia and Pulmonary Oedema — Differential Discrimination
chunks.text:
one of the highest-value judgements in acute chest medicine, and one of
the most frequently made incorrectly. ## Findings favouring cardiogenic oedema
- Cardiomegaly (projection-sensitive; over-estimated on supine AP films)
- Perihilar, central "bat-wing" alveolar distribution
- Kerley B lines, subpleural septal thickening, fissural thickening
- Pleural effusions
- Elevated natriuretic peptides
- Clinical volume overload: raised JVP, peripheral oedema, positive fluid balance
- Known left ventricular dysfunction, ischaemic heart disease, valvular disease ## Findings favouring pneumonia - Focal or multifocal lobar consolidation
- Air bronchograms within an opaque lobe
- Fever, pleuritic pain, focal crepitations
- Productive cough, sputum purulence
- Elevated inflammatory markers with a compatible syndrome
- Raised white cell count with a leftward shift ## Findings that do not discriminate

chunks.title: Pneumonia and Pulmonary Oedema — Differential Discrimination
chunks.text:
ulence
- Elevated inflammatory markers with a compatible syndrome
- Raised white cell count with a leftward shift ## Findings that do not discriminate
- Bilateral infiltrates: present in both
- Hypoxaemia: present in both
- Elevated CRP: present in both, and in many other inflammatory conditions
- Ground-glass attenuation: present in both
- Older age: present in both
- Reduced lung expansion: present in both ## The strongest discriminators The discriminators that survive scrutiny are the *distributional* ones —
cardiac silhouette size, perihilar vs peripheral distribution, septal lines,
effusions — supported by clinical volume status. Biomarkers discriminate least. ## Overlap "Mixed" patterns are common. A patient with ischaemic heart disease may develop
aspiration pneumonia; a patient with pneumonia may develop acute kidney injury
and volume overload. Forcing every presentation into a single label is a
recognisable failure mode. ## Practice point

chunks.title: Pneumonia and Pulmonary Oedema — Differential Discrimination
chunks.text:
may develop acute kidney injury
and volume overload. Forcing every presentation into a single label is a
recognisable failure mode. ## Practice point
Where the clinical and radiological pictures disagree, escalate rather than
resolve artificially. Serial imaging and clinical reassessment carry more
information than a single cross-sectional moment.

chunks.title: Radiology Reference — Chest Radiograph Patterns of Parenchymal Opacity
chunks.text:
# Radiology Reference — Chest Radiograph Patterns of Parenchymal Opacity PROVENANCE: Local reference note authored for the MedExplain AI research prototype. Not a published article, not a verbatim society guideline, no PMID or DOI. Included so the retrieval pipeline has real local material to search. ## Ground-glass opacity Ground-glass opacity describes a region of increased lung attenuation that
**does not obscure underlying bronchial and vascular markings**. This single
distinguishing feature separates it from consolidation, which obscures them. Important limitation: ground-glass attenuation is a *descriptive imaging
pattern*, not a diagnosis. The same appearance arises from many processes —
infection, interstitial inflammation, interstitial oedema, haemorrhage,
aspiration, and artefact such as underpenetration or motion. ## Distribution

chunks.title: Radiology Reference — Chest Radiograph Patterns of Parenchymal Opacity
chunks.text:
—
infection, interstitial inflammation, interstitial oedema, haemorrhage,
aspiration, and artefact such as underpenetration or motion. ## Distribution
- **Bilateral, peripheral, subpleural, basilar** distribution: seen in acute
  interstitial processes and in many viral pneumonias; also described in acute
  eosinophilic injury and in some non-infectious interstitial conditions. - **Bilateral, diffuse, central/perihilar** ("bat-wing") distribution: more
  typical of alveolar oedema. - **Focal lobar consolidation**: typical of bacterial pneumonia but not specific. Distribution is a *probability-shaping* observation. It changes the probability
of a differential; it does not establish one. ## Cardiomegaly An increased cardiothoracic ratio suggests cardiogenic aetiology, but projection
and inspiratory effort significantly affect the measurement. Portable
supine films commonly exaggerate the ratio. ## Pleural effusions Small bilateral effusions are common in both cardiogenic and non-cardiogenic
processes.

chunks.title: Radiology Reference — Chest Radiograph Patterns of Parenchymal Opacity
chunks.text:
pine films commonly exaggerate the ratio. ## Pleural effusions Small bilateral effusions are common in both cardiogenic and non-cardiogenic
processes.
Large unilateral effusions are more suggestive of a unilateral
process (parapneumonic, malignant, or congestive). ## Technical adequacy Before any pattern is described, image adequacy must be assessed: 1. Rotation — the spinous processes should be equidistant from the medial
   clavicular heads. 2. Inspiration — at least 8-10 posterior ribs should be visible. 3. Penetration — thoracic vertebrae should be just visible through the heart. 4. Collimation and motion. An inadequate study limits the strength of any description, and the limitation
should be stated explicitly rather than silently interpreted. ## What a radiograph cannot establish A single projection cannot establish temporal change, depth, enhancement
behaviour, or the nature of an underlying process. Comparison with prior
imaging and cross-sectional imaging are frequently required.

chunks.title: Voice and Speech Recording — Clinical Data Quality Note
chunks.text:
# Voice and Speech Recording — Clinical Data Quality Note PROVENANCE: Local reference note authored for the MedExplain AI research prototype. Not a published article, no PMID or DOI. Included so the retrieval pipeline has
real local material to search. Relevant because the pipeline's acoustic
features are only interpretable under stated conditions. ## Recording conditions matter Speech-based clinical capture is only as reliable as its recording conditions. Key variables: - **Ambient noise floor** — background noise degrades word error rate sharply. A noise floor within roughly 10 dB of the speech level causes severe
  degradation; within 20 dB causes measurable but usable degradation. - **Signal-to-noise ratio** is a better predictor of transcript reliability than
  absolute volume. - **Microphone distance** — a consistent 15-20 cm working distance keeps level
  stable.

chunks.title: Voice and Speech Recording — Clinical Data Quality Note
chunks.text:
r predictor of transcript reliability than
  absolute volume. - **Microphone distance** — a consistent 15-20 cm working distance keeps level
  stable.
Unconstrained distance is a common source of level variation. - **Room reverberation** blurs formants, particularly the second formant, and
  degrades phoneme discrimination. ## Consequences for acoustic features The pipeline's acoustic features are computed on the decoded waveform. They
are only interpretable when the recording conditions are adequate: - **Zero-crossing rate** is inversely related to dominant frequency. It is
  strongly speaker- and channel-dependent, and microphone high-pass filtering
  removes the lowest-frequency crossings. - **Spectral centroid** is the balance point of the power spectrum. It rises with
  brightness and with harshness, and is also strongly channel-dependent. - **Spectral flatness** approaches 1 for noise and falls with tonal content. It is frequently the best single indicator of an un-usable recording.

chunks.title: Voice and Speech Recording — Clinical Data Quality Note
chunks.text:
nt. - **Spectral flatness** approaches 1 for noise and falls with tonal content. It is frequently the best single indicator of an un-usable recording.
- **Spectral rolloff (85%)** marks the frequency below which 85% of energy lies. It rises with bandwidth. Because these features are channel-dependent, they support **recording-quality
gating** and **prosody (contour, tempo, pause) assessment**. They do **not**
support diagnostic claims about voice pathology. Voice quality indices such as
jitter and shimmer computed on a consumer microphone are not clinically valid. ## Telemetry is more reliable than features For deciding whether a recording is usable, the proportion of non-speech
("silence") frames, the SNR estimate, and the spectral flatness summary are more
robust than any single feature vector. ## Clinical safety An automatically produced transcript is a **draft for confirmation**, not a
record of what the patient said. Any clinical decision that depends on the
transcript must be checked against the clinician's own documentation.
